body:
Scope: independent Delivery rereview of the complete amended primary plan with added M3. M1/M2 remain their previously reviewed criteria implementation and bounded protection-preserving audit. M3 follows the user's subsequent explicit selection of historical lifecycle protocols and cache applicability tests for removal; it is an intentional coverage exception, not evidence that those tests are redundant or that supported runtime contracts are retired.

Authority and claim boundary: the direct user scope amendment takes precedence over the original proposal's bounded cleanup set and ordinary TEST-SR-08 protection-preservation condition for the specifically selected tests. This review therefore does not assert that M3 satisfies the ordinary equivalent-proof-or-retired-behavior removal criterion. The Test model remains valid general policy, and its earlier approval is not retargeted to bless reduced coverage. This exception is bounded to the plan's thirteen files and eleven cache methods; absent a user answer to broader cache clarification, no authority for broader cache/storage/hash/serialization removal is inferred. M3 preserves runtime commands, schemas and all unlisted tests/fixtures/helpers, apart from imports proven unused solely by the deletion.

Allocation and feasibility: pass within that explicit exception. Independently inspected the selected files and cache definitions; all thirteen file paths and eleven method names exist. The remaining fourteen cache methods retain the allocated hashing, path-normalization, identity and record-shape/serialization scope. Package node --test discovery and Python unittest discovery support deleting the selected test definitions without a new runner. Bounded search found no direct runner/import dependency on the selected file names in scripts, GitHub workflows or unselected test modules. Historical spec/test-spec references remain historical evidence, not an assertion those removed focused commands still work.

Coverage-loss assessment: selected protocol tests include final-verification vocabulary/freshness rules, package settlement/routing, ownership, migration/repair, transaction rollback/interruption, read-only observations and historical workflow transitions. Selected cache methods cover eligibility restrictions, unsafe lookup inputs, missing/unresolvable implementation dependencies, branch/worktree scope, matching-pass reuse, helper/policy invalidation and cache-only final-verification limits. These are real protections for still-present behavior; remaining green tests cannot prove the deleted obligations. The plan explicitly preserves this limitation and does not falsely retire runtime support or claim complete absence of all overlapping coverage.

Sequence and verification: pass. M3 waits for its independent allocation review; implementation verifies exact definitions/imports, removes only selected cases, compares baseline/result discovery and unchanged remaining definitions, runs complete remaining Node/cache suites, records losses and obtains milestone review. The named Node/cache commands are valid repository entrypoints; supplied baseline counts are 166 selected historical runtime cases (164 passed, two skipped) and 25 cache tests, not post-removal success. TG-05 requires actual resulting counts and exact attribution, so incidental discovery loss cannot be hidden by the deliberately reduced count. New failures return to the owning correction or blocker rather than expanding deletion. Restore preceding selected files/methods if rollback is needed.

Complete-plan coherence: M1/M2 requirement/hazard allocations remain applicable only to their original scope. TG-FINAL-01 now distinguishes their ordinary maintenance claims from M3's user-selected coverage exception, and the final checkpoint depends on M1/M2/M3 plus corrections. The plan requires full-range PR-mode checks before renewed closeout, fresh independent final whole-change review and distinct Verify with explicit reduced-protection limits. Prior final/Verify judgments remain restricted; unchanged skill/adapter evidence may be reused only on affirmative current-source/environment basis. No automatic continuation, work initialization, runtime retirement or external permission follows from this recording.

No material allocation or necessary-owner-decision finding prevents this exact user-selected work. Approval is a scoped judgment that the requested exception is bounded, executable and honestly verifiable; it is not a claim that loss of regression coverage improves engineering confidence. If the implementation broadens paths/methods, changes runtime behavior or conceals lost protection, this judgment does not apply. Return at the isolated Delivery-review boundary.
independence_basis: Separate nonauthor delegated agent /root/independent_proposal_review assessed the M3 amendment and actual selected test definitions. The author drafted the plan from the user instruction; this reviewer authored no plan or engineering changes and writes only its own renewed assessment. Prior independent reviews are not authorship of the expanded scope.
